newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX drops after Issing comments, SAP falls.
newsitem.headline: German DAX drops after Issing comments, SAP falls.

text.p: German shares dived in post-bourse electronic trading, after the Bundesbank's chief economist Olmar Issing said he saw no reason to expect lower key German interest rates, putting pressure on German bonds.
The IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day computer trade in the DAX index of 30 leading shares, dropped over 20 points on Issing's comments to trade down 44.15 points, or 1.62 percent, at 2,677.59.

The DAX had already come under pressure during floor trade after one of its leading components, business software firm SAP AG, fell over 23 percent on a profit warning. The DAX ended bourse trade down 19.45 points, or 0.72 percent, at 2,699.53.

SAP preference shares dived over 23 percent to end bourse trade down 65.90 marks at 212 marks, after the group stunned markets on Tuesday evening with an unexpectedly sharp slowdown in growth in the third quarter.
The third quarter figures forced SAP to revise down its 1996 revenue forecast to 3.5 billion marks from the 3.8 billion marks previously expected.

Dietmar Hopp, chief executive of the company which had been the darling of the DAX index, said the market's reaction to the firm's profit warning was exaggerated and said a cut in the dividend was "unthinkable".
Although most attention was centered on SAP, dealers said there would be some interest in the banking sector ahead of the nine-month reports of certain banks.
"If there is disappointment in those results, then the market could really suffer," said one dealer.
Deutsche Bank is due to publish nine-month results on Thursday, followed by Bayerische Vereinsbank on Friday.
German car maker Volkswagen AG was boosted after the firm said its pre-tax profit soared 56.2 percent during the first nine months of the year on what has been strong sales growth.
Group pre-tax profit for the first nine months of 1996 was 1.481 billion marks, up from 948 million marks for the same period last year.
VW shares were up 4.45 marks at 585.70 in post-bourse trade against the market trend.
Meanwhile, Swiss-controlled German retail giant Metro AG fell nearly five percent after the firm released a pessimistic sales forecast. The stock was down 6.35 points to 126.65 marks in IBIS trade.
